narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model behind the decision predicts a 72% chance you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. In plain terms, you were seen as more likely to fail than to pass, and the admissions committee used that signal to avoid accepting a student who might never become a licensed attorney.

The most powerful factor was your Year 3 class ranking. You finished in the bottom 10% of your cohort, while accepted students typically sit near the middle. That low ranking, after three years of study, is a strong warning that your academic foundation remains shaky, and it pushed the prediction hard
